explanation: The theorem says the m-th coefficient of the finite product ∏_{n∈s}(1 - X^(n+1)) over ℤ⟦X⟧ is the same for every finset s containing range (m+1). I grepped Mathlib's PowerSeries, Combinatorics and NumberTheory directories for coefficient-of-product lemmas and for 1 - X^(n+1) products. The closest hit is PowerSeries.coeff_prod_one_sub_X_pow_eventually_eq in Mathlib/Combinatorics/Enumerative/Pentagonal/PowerSeries.lean. It only says that, eventually along atTop on finsets, the coefficient equals the pentagonal series coefficient. The threshold finset is not given explicitly, so it does not give the explicit bound s ⊇ range (m+1). Mathlib also has multipliable_one_sub_X_pow and related lemmas, but none states this stability for a concrete s. The library's own proof uses local helpers (Cong.prod, Cong.one_sub_X_pow, coeff_mul_of_cong) that do not appear in Mathlib.
